mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased corporate revenues and earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic output and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO declines by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a single month signals strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increases by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for two consecutive months signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS decreases for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate margins.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high level of real GDP (GDPC1) relative to its 12-month moving average signals strong economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate continued economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 is above its 12-month moving average.
